title: John Paul II (1978–2005)
hookLine: a pope from Poland who opened his papacy crying be not afraid

lines: A NEW POPE, A FULL SQUARE.
cards: Saint Peter's Square, packed. The new pope stands before the crowd at the Mass that begins his papacy: broad-shouldered, a former actor with a voice that carries.

He comes from a country behind the Iron Curtain, under a communist government wary of the Church. Partway through his homily he says it, then says it again: be not afraid. Open wide the doors for Christ.
Open the borders of states, of economic and political systems. Do not be afraid. His name was Karol Wojtyła.
He took the name John Paul.

teach.b: Those words weren't a slogan dreamed up on the day. They came out of a life. Loss came first.

Karol grew up in a small Polish town, and by the time he was a young man his mother, his only brother and his father had all died. Then the occupation. When Nazi Germany occupied Poland, the universities were shut.

He worked in a stone quarry and a chemical plant, acted in an underground theater that performed in people's living rooms, and studied for the priesthood in a secret seminary. Any of it could have cost him his life.
As priest and then archbishop of Kraków, under a communist government, he hiked and skied and kayaked with students, taught philosophy, and pushed for churches the state didn't want built.
So when he said be not afraid, he spoke as someone who had been afraid with good reason, and had gone on anyway.

teach.h: THE WORDS COME FROM THE WATER.
teach.b: The words belong to the Gospels first.

teach.h: BE OF GOOD HEART: IT IS I, FEAR YE NOT.
teach.b: When the disciples see Jesus walking toward them on the water at night and cry out in terror, he says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Be of good heart: it is I, fear ye not."

John Paul's papacy was long and sometimes argued over, and the coming days look at a few of its moments. But the opening note was this one: the fear is real, and the voice on the water speaks to it anyway.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint John Paul II, and his words be not afraid are often sung, printed on banners, and quoted at confirmations and youth gatherings.

games.q: you're young Karol in occupied Poland. the theaters and universities are shut. what do you do?
o: stop acting and studying until the war is over.
act in an underground theater and study in a secret seminary.
games.why: he worked in a quarry by day, acted in living rooms and studied in secret, at real risk.

practice: Let one thing come to mind that you've been putting off because it scares you: a conversation, an apology, a doctor's appointment, saying no, saying yes.
Notice where the fear sits in your body, breathe there, and shrink the brave thing down to its first small step. If you pray, pray the line from the water: be of good heart, fear ye not.

wordCard.voice: Secret seminary. Where Karol Wojtyła studied for the priesthood in secret during the Nazi occupation of Poland, before he became Pope John Paul the Second and said be not afraid.

carryVoice: Your line: be not afraid. A man who knew loss and danger said it first to a full square. Rest well.
